We made a fifteen second test for Coca-Cola. Nobody asked us to.

Here is what happened. A trend was going around online. We looked at it, thought it had one good film in it, and decided to find out if we were right.

So we wrote it, built it, and made the whole thing with AI. No crew call, no location, no bottle wrangler with a spray bottle of glycerine. Just a concept, a lot of iterations, and a team that knows what a commercial is supposed to feel like before it ever reaches a screen.

That last part matters more than the tools. AI does not give you taste. It gives you options. Knowing which option is the film, that is still the job.

The result is fifteen seconds that look like a proper spot. Casting, wardrobe, grade, sound. A haircut that deserves its own agent.

To be clear, this is a test, not a campaign. We do this because we want to know what these tools can actually carry. Not in a demo. In a real brief, with a real brand, with real standards. Now we know. They can carry quite a lot, as long as somebody is steering.

If you work at Coca-Cola, or you know someone who does, send this their way. We would love to hear what they think. Even if what they think is no.

And if you are a brand or an agency sitting on an idea that feels too expensive to shoot, come talk to us. There is a decent chance it is not too expensive anymore.

ROKU Films. Amsterdam.

The group chat has been trying to plan padel since March. It's October.

So we built EffePadelle. You make a competition in three taps, share one link, and everyone's in. Same partner all season, or a new one every round.

The app sorts the rest. Who plays who, and an evening everyone is actually free.

Swipe to see how it works. We're live today in the App Store and on Google Play. Free to start.
